title: 实验 3-6 · 运放积分器：方波变三角波
summary: 用 LM358（单电源 9 V）搭一个反相积分器：方波输入变成三角波输出，由三角波的斜率测出 RC；正弦输入则输出余弦。
concepts: 直流反馈电阻 DC feedback resistor
description: **目标**：用 LM358 搭一个反相积分器，看方波积分成三角波，并和实验 3-2 的 RC 积分电路比较。
**电路**（LM358 用 A 半或 B 半都行）：
- 电源：9 V 接 8 脚 V+，GND 接 4 脚 V−。
- 偏置：RB1（10 kΩ）从 +9 V 到 IN+，RB2（10 kΩ）从 IN+ 到 GND，IN+ 被定在 VREF = 4.5 V（电源中点）。
- 输入：信号发生器红夹子 → CIN（10 µF，隔直）→ RIN（10 kΩ）→ IN−。黑夹子接 GND。
- 反馈：CF（100 nF）接在 IN− 和 OUT 之间；RP（100 kΩ）和 CF 并联。
**信号发生器**：方波，幅度 1 V、偏置 0，频率 1 kHz。**示波器**：CH1 看信号发生器输出，CH2 看运放 OUT。
**为什么需要这些“辅助”元件**：
- **RB1/RB2**：单电源运放的输出只能在 0 ~ 7.5 V（V+ − 1.5 V）之间，所以把参考点抬到 4.5 V，三角波才能上下摆动。
- **CIN**：信号发生器的输出以 GND 为中心，而 IN− 在 4.5 V；CIN 隔开这 4.5 V 的直流差（CIN·RIN = 0.1 s，对 1 kHz 来说就是一根导线）。
- **RP**：电容对直流开路，没有 RP 时运放在直流下是开环的，任何一点点直流误差都会被一直积分下去，输出很快撞到电源轨不动了（在仿真里会卡在 7.5 V）。RP 给直流一条反馈路径（直流增益 −RP/RIN = −10），代价是低频时不再是理想积分。
**先预测**：通电之前先自己算：输出三角波的斜率、Vpp 和中心电压各是多少？输入为正时输出往哪边走？思路：虚短让 IN− 跟着 IN+ 保持在 4.5 V，虚断让流过 RIN 的电流 i = u_i/RIN 全部流进 CF，所以 u_o − 4.5 V = −(1/(RIN·CF))∫u_i dt；斜率 = 输入电压/(RIN·CF)，再乘以半周期。
**测量**：在示波器上读 OUT 的 Vpp、中心电压，以及输入为正的半周期里输出的变化方向；再试试 2 kHz 方波、1 kHz 正弦和 100 Hz 方波。电路检查通过后，把读数填进下面的「测量」（以你自己的面包板为准）；答完后会显示计算对比。
**真实电路里**：
- 10 µF 的 CIN 一般是铝电解电容，有极性：+ 脚要接直流电位高的一侧。这里信号发生器一侧的直流是 0 V，IN− 一侧是 4.5 V，所以 + 脚朝 RIN / IN−。接反的电解电容漏电变大，时间长了会发热甚至损坏。仿真里的电容没有极性，接反不会报错。
- LM358 的输入共模范围只到约 V+ − 1.5 V（这里 7.5 V），IN+ = 4.5 V 在范围内；输出摆不到正电源轨（仿真也把输出限制在 V+ − 1.5 V）。它的压摆率约 0.3–0.5 V/µs、增益带宽积约 1 MHz，仿真没有这两项限制；这个实验里三角波的斜率只有 0.001 V/µs，频率也低，离这些极限很远。

en.title: Experiment 3-6 · Op-amp integrator: square in, triangle out
en.summary: Build an inverting integrator from an LM358 (single 9 V supply): a square wave in gives a triangle out, whose slope measures RC; a sine in gives a cosine out.
description: **Goal**: build an inverting integrator with an LM358, watch a square wave integrate into a triangle, and compare it with the RC integrator of Experiment 3-2.
**Circuit** (either half of the LM358 is fine):
- Power: 9 V to pin 8 (V+), GND to pin 4 (V−).
- Bias: RB1 (10 kΩ) from +9 V to IN+, RB2 (10 kΩ) from IN+ to GND, fixing IN+ at VREF = 4.5 V (mid-supply).
- Input: generator red clip → CIN (10 µF, DC block) → RIN (10 kΩ) → IN−. Black clip to GND.
- Feedback: CF (100 nF) between IN− and OUT; RP (100 kΩ) in parallel with CF.
**Generator**: square wave, amplitude 1 V, offset 0, 1 kHz. **Scope**: CH1 on the generator output, CH2 on the op-amp OUT.
**Why the "helper" parts are needed**:
- **RB1/RB2**: a single-supply op-amp output can only move between 0 and 7.5 V (V+ − 1.5 V), so the reference is lifted to 4.5 V to give the triangle room to swing both ways.
- **CIN**: the generator output is centred on GND, but IN− sits at 4.5 V; CIN blocks that 4.5 V DC difference (CIN·RIN = 0.1 s, so at 1 kHz it is just a wire).

- **RP**: a capacitor is open at DC, so without RP the op-amp runs open-loop at DC and integrates any tiny DC error forever — the output soon hits a rail and stays there (in the simulator it sticks at 7.5 V). RP gives DC a feedback path (DC gain −RP/RIN = −10); the price is a less-than-ideal integrator at low frequencies.

**Predict first**: before powering up, work out the slope, Vpp and centre voltage of the output triangle, and which way the output moves while the input is positive. Method: the virtual short holds IN− at the same 4.5 V as IN+ and the inputs draw no current, so the current through RIN, i = u_i/RIN, all flows into CF and u_o − 4.5 V = −(1/(RIN·CF))∫u_i dt; slope = input voltage/(RIN·CF), then multiply by half a period.

**Measure**: read the Vpp and centre of OUT on the scope, and which way the output moves during the positive half of the input; then try a 2 kHz square, a 1 kHz sine and a 100 Hz square. Once the circuit check passes, type your readings into the Measurements below (whatever your own board shows); the worked comparison appears after you answer.
**In a real circuit**:

- A 10 µF part like CIN is usually an aluminium electrolytic, which is polarised: its + lead must sit at the higher DC potential. Here the generator side is at 0 V DC and the IN− side at 4.5 V, so + faces RIN / IN−. A reversed electrolytic leaks, heats up and can fail over time. The simulated capacitor has no polarity, so a reversed one is not flagged.

- The LM358's input common-mode range only reaches about V+ − 1.5 V (7.5 V here), so IN+ = 4.5 V is fine; its output cannot reach the positive rail (the simulator also clamps it at V+ − 1.5 V). Its slew rate is about 0.3–0.5 V/µs and its gain-bandwidth product about 1 MHz, neither of which the simulator models; in this experiment the triangle's slope is only 0.001 V/µs and the frequency is low, far from those limits.
compare: **Compare**: with a ±1 V square wave the output ramps at a constant slope of 1 V/(10 kΩ × 100 nF) = 1000 V/s for each half period, covering 0.5 V in 0.5 ms: **the output is a 0.5 Vpp triangle centred on 4.5 V**, falling while the input is positive (inverting). At 1 kHz, RP·CF = 10 ms is far longer than half a period and RP's effect is hardly visible. If the output sits at 7.5 V or 0 V, check that the feedback goes to IN− and that RP is in place.

**Think about it**: compared with the RC integrator of Experiment 3-2, the RC circuit only "looks like" an integrator when τ ≫ T, and its output is tiny; the op-amp integrator uses the virtual short so the resistor current doesn't depend on the output, giving a true integral over a wide frequency range and a large output.
- 2 kHz square: same slope, half the time, so Vpp halves to ≈ 0.25 V.

- 1 kHz sine (1 V amplitude): integrating sin gives −cos, so the output is a sine of the same frequency with amplitude 1 V/(ωRC) = 1/(2π × 1000 × 1 ms) ≈ 0.16 V (≈ 0.32 Vpp), leading the input by about 90° (inversion 180° + integration −90°; RP adds about 1°, so the scope reads about 91°).

- 100 Hz square: the 5 ms half period is now comparable with RP·CF = 10 ms and RP shows: the edges turn exponential and Vpp ≈ 2 × 10 × tanh(T/(4·RP·CF)) ≈ 4.9 V, far below the 10 V an ideal integrator would give.

measurements.ask: 1 kHz square: the Vpp of the CH2 (OUT) triangle
measurements.explain: Slope 1 V / (RIN·CF) = 1000 V/s; a 0.5 ms half period covers 0.5 V.

measurements.ask: Slope = 1 V / (RIN·CF), and one 0.5 ms half period covers Vpp. From your Vpp, RIN·CF = 1 V × 0.5 ms / Vpp
measurements.explain: 10 kΩ × 100 nF = 1 ms. Unlike the RC integrator, the op-amp keeps the resistor current independent of the output, so the slope is always input / RC.

measurements.ask: Same state: multimeter DC range, OUT to GND (the centre of the triangle)
measurements.explain: The virtual short keeps IN− at IN+ = 4.5 V; RP gives DC feedback, and its gain of −10 acts on a 0 V average input, so the centre is 4.5 V.

measurements.ask: On the scope: while the input is positive, which way does the output move?
measurements.explain: The current u_i / RIN flows into IN− and on into CF, pulling the OUT side down: u_o − 4.5 V = −(1/RC)∫u_i dt. The phase relative to the input is +90° (inversion 180° + integration −90°).

measurements.ask: 100 Hz square: OUT Vpp (compare with the ideal integrator's 10 V)
measurements.explain: A 5 ms half period is comparable with RP·CF = 10 ms, so RP shows: 2 × 10 × tanh(T/(4·RP·CF)) ≈ 4.9 V.

hints: Power first: pin 8 to +9 V, pin 4 to GND. The chip must straddle the centre gap.
RB1 and RB2 form a divider whose middle goes to IN+ (4.5 V).
CF and RP both go between IN− and OUT (in parallel); the input path is generator → CIN → RIN → IN−.
tests: 1 kHz square: a triangle centred on VREF, about +90° from the input
2 kHz square: half the time, half the height
1 kHz sine: integral of a sine is a (−)cosine, about +90°
100 Hz square: RP's leak shows — smaller than an ideal integrator, no clipping

tests.name: 1 kHz 方波：三角波，中心在 VREF，相对输入约 +90°
2 kHz 方波：时间减半，三角波高度减半
1 kHz 正弦：正弦的积分是（负）余弦，约 +90°
100 Hz 方波：RP 的“漏电”显现，比理想积分小，且不削顶

compare: **对比**：方波 ±1 V 时，每半周期输出以恒定斜率 1 V/(10 kΩ × 100 nF) = 1000 V/s 直线变化，半周期 0.5 ms 走 0.5 V：**输出是 0.5 Vpp 的三角波，中心 4.5 V**，输入为正时输出下降（反相）。在 1 kHz，RP·CF = 10 ms 远大于半周期，RP 的影响几乎看不出。如果输出贴在 7.5 V 或 0 V 不动，检查反馈是否接到 IN−、RP 有没有接上。
**想一想**：和实验 3-2 的 RC 积分电路比：RC 电路要求 τ ≫ T 才“像”积分，输出也很小；运放积分器靠虚短让电阻电流不受输出影响，在很宽的频率范围里都是真正的积分，幅度可以做大。
- 2 kHz 方波：三角波斜率不变，时间减半，Vpp 减半到 ≈ 0.25 V。
- 1 kHz 正弦（幅度 1 V）：积分 sin 得到 −cos，输出是同频正弦，幅度 1 V/(ωRC) = 1/(2π × 1000 × 1 ms) ≈ 0.16 V（≈ 0.32 Vpp），相位超前输入约 90°（反相 180° + 积分 −90°；RP 让它多出约 1°，示波器读数约 91°）。
- 100 Hz 方波：半周期 5 ms 已经和 RP·CF = 10 ms 相当，RP 的影响出来了——边沿变成指数曲线，Vpp ≈ 2 × 10 × tanh(T/(4·RP·CF)) ≈ 4.9 V，比理想积分的 10 V 小得多。

measurements.ask: 1 kHz 方波：CH2（OUT）三角波的 Vpp
measurements.explain: 斜率 1 V / (RIN·CF) = 1000 V/s，半周期 0.5 ms 走 0.5 V。

measurements.ask: 斜率 = 1 V / (RIN·CF)，半周期 0.5 ms 走完 Vpp。用你的 Vpp 算 RIN·CF = 1 V × 0.5 ms / Vpp
measurements.explain: 10 kΩ × 100 nF = 1 ms。和 RC 积分电路不同，运放让电阻电流不受输出影响，所以斜率始终是输入 / RC。

measurements.ask: 同一状态：万用表直流档测 OUT 对 GND（三角波的中心）
measurements.explain: 虚短让 IN− 跟着 IN+ = 4.5 V；RP 给直流提供反馈，直流增益 −10 作用在 0 V 的平均输入上，所以中心就是 4.5 V。

measurements.ask: 在示波器上看：输入为正的半周期里，输出往哪边走？
measurements.explain: 电流 u_i / RIN 从输入流进 IN−，全部流进 CF，把 OUT 一侧往下拉：u_o − 4.5 V = −(1/RC)∫u_i dt。相对输入的相位是 +90°（反相 180° + 积分 −90°）。

measurements.ask: 100 Hz 方波：OUT 的 Vpp（和“理想积分”的 10 V 比）
measurements.explain: 半周期 5 ms 已和 RP·CF = 10 ms 相当，RP 的影响出来了：2 × 10 × tanh(T/(4·RP·CF)) ≈ 4.9 V。

hints: 先供电：8 脚接 +9 V，4 脚接 GND。芯片要横跨中间凹槽。
RB1、RB2 组成分压器，中点接 IN+（4.5 V）。
CF 和 RP 都接在 IN− 和 OUT 之间（并联）；输入路径是 信号发生器 → CIN → RIN → IN−。
